authority_citations: REQ-SAG-0601 v2 statement: A request that receives an HTTP 429, 502 or 529 response must be resent until a configurable maximum number of sends, 5 by default, is reached.
REQ-SAG-0601 v2 quote: A request that receives a busy response MUST be resent unchanged.
REQ-SAG-0601 v2 scope: adds or changes busy-response handling, resend, holdoff or the runner queue
phase-a-intent v1: shared HTTP layer is in plan scope

item.text: A request answered 429 is resent unchanged until max_sends (default 5) is reached, then returns http.provider_busy.
item.title: Busy resend

cases.rationale: Approved pass fixture of the locked anchor: resend of a busy response up to a configurable max_sends with default 5.

item.text: A 429 response is returned to the caller at once and never resent.
item.title: Busy handling

cases.rationale: Approved fail fixture: never resending a 429 is irreconcilable with the statement's must-resend rule; it does not carry the directive.

item.text: The shared HTTP client treats HTTP 429, 502 and 529 as busy responses. A busy request is resent unchanged until it has been sent max_sends times; max_sends is configurable and defaults to 5. When the limit is reached the client returns http.provider_busy. The holdoff between sends is applied in the runner queue.
item.title: Shared HTTP busy resend

cases.rationale: States every element of the statement: the three statuses, resend, configurable maximum number of sends, default 5.

item.text: Implement the shared HTTP send path for TypeSafe requests and the runner queue that dispatches a batch of decision requests in parallel, with per-request timeouts and session logging of every send.
item.title: Runner queue and send path

cases.rationale: Changes the send path and the runner queue (named in scope) but says nothing about busy responses or resend; silence is not conflict.

item.text: The HTTP layer will handle busy and rate-limit responses from providers gracefully so that consumers see fewer failures.
item.title: Provider error handling

cases.rationale: Names the topic (busy responses) but carries none of the directive's specific content: no resend, no maximum number of sends, no default; a vague intent neither carries nor breaks the rule.

item.text: On HTTP 529 or 502 the client fails fast: the error is surfaced to the caller immediately and the request is not retried; retrying is left to consumer code.
item.title: Fail fast on overload

cases.rationale: The statement requires 502 and 529 responses to be resent by the layer; never resending them cannot be reconciled with it and the directive is absent.

item.text: Define the DecisionId newtype in sc-agent-types with a serde representation as a lowercase UUID string and Display/FromStr implementations.
item.title: DecisionId newtype

cases.rationale: A type definition unrelated to busy-response handling, resend, holdoff or the runner queue.

item.text: Busy responses (HTTP 429, 502, 529) are resent with holdoff from the runner queue. A request is sent at most max_sends times (configurable, default 5): if the fifth send is also answered busy, the request is not sent a sixth time and the call returns http.provider_busy.
item.title: Send limit exhaustion

cases.rationale: Boundary of the limit: stopping after the fifth send at the default is exactly 'until a configurable maximum number of sends, 5 by default, is reached'.

item.text: Busy responses (HTTP 429, 502 and 529) are resent until max_sends, configurable with default 5, is reached. Other errors such as HTTP 400, 401 and 500 are not busy responses and are returned to the caller immediately without resend.
item.title: Non-busy errors

cases.rationale: The statement only governs 429, 502 and 529; not resending other statuses is outside it and does not conflict, while the busy rule is carried.
